pharm: Long-acting PDE5 inhibitor; enhances nitric oxide/cGMP-mediated smooth muscle relaxation in the corpus cavernosum, prostate, bladder, and pulmonary vasculature
quick: ED PRN: 10 mg before activity (5-20 mg); once-daily ED 2.5-5 mg; BPH or ED/BPH 5 mg daily; PAH 40 mg daily
May take with or without food; absorption not affected
Not indicated in females; no human pregnancy data
Not indicated in females; present in milk of lactating rats
CrCl 30-50: lower/spaced PRN dosing; CrCl <30 or dialysis: PRN max 5 mg/72 h, daily not recommended
Mild/moderate (Child-Pugh A/B): adjust/limit dose; severe (Child-Pugh C): not recommended
Substantial intake (>=5 units) with tadalafil may cause orthostatic hypotension, tachycardia, dizziness
Blood pressure/cardiovascular status; vision/hearing changes; prolonged erection
summary: Tadalafil is a long-acting oral PDE5 inhibitor indicated for erectile dysfunction (ED), the signs and symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), ED with concurrent BPH (ED/BPH), and (as the Adcirca brand) pulmonary arterial hypertension. For ED it may be used on demand (10 mg, range 5-20 mg, before activity) or once daily (2.5-5 mg); BPH and ED/BPH are treated with 5 mg once daily; PAH is treated with 40 mg once daily. Its long ~17.5-hour half-life supports effect up to 36 hours after an on-demand dose. It is absolutely contraindicated with organic nitrates in any form and with guanylate cyclase stimulators such as riociguat due to life-threatening hypotension. Notable risks include hypotension (additive with alpha-blockers, antihypertensives, and alcohol), non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), sudden hearing loss, and priapism.
indications: Signs and symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH)
ED with concurrent signs and symptoms of BPH (ED/BPH)
Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, WHO Group 1) to improve exercise ability (Adcirca brand)

May be taken with or without food
PRN dosing: take prior to anticipated sexual activity; requires sexual stimulation to be effective
Once-daily dosing (ED, BPH, ED/BPH): take at approximately the same time each day
PAH (Adcirca): take both 20 mg tablets together once daily

Available as 2.5, 5, 10, and 20 mg film-coated tablets
moa: Penile erection during sexual stimulation depends on nitric oxide (NO) release in the corpus cavernosum, which activates guanylate cyclase to increase cyclic GMP (cGMP), causing smooth muscle relaxation and increased blood inflow. Tadalafil selectively inhibits phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5), the enzyme that degrades cGMP, thereby raising cGMP and enhancing the NO-mediated erectile response; it has no effect in the absence of sexual stimulation. The same PDE5 inhibition affects cGMP in smooth muscle of the prostate, bladder, and their vascular supply (relevant to BPH, though the exact mechanism of symptom relief is not established) and in the pulmonary vasculature, producing vasodilation that underlies its use in PAH. Tadalafil is highly selective for PDE5 over other phosphodiesterases.

absolute: Concurrent use of organic nitrates in any form (regular or intermittent) - potentiates the hypotensive effect of nitrates
Concurrent guanylate cyclase (GC) stimulators such as riociguat - additive hypotension
Known serious hypersensitivity to tadalafil or ADCIRCA (including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, exfoliative dermatitis)
relative: Conditions in which sexual activity is inadvisable due to underlying cardiovascular status
Left ventricular outflow obstruction (e.g., aortic stenosis, idiopathic hypertrophic subaortic stenosis) - sensitivity to vasodilators
Concurrent alpha-blockers, antihypertensives, or substantial alcohol (>=5 units) - risk of symptomatic hypotension
Not recommended with alpha-blockers for BPH treatment; caution when used for ED in men on alpha-blockers
Conditions predisposing to priapism (sickle cell anemia, multiple myeloma, leukemia) or anatomic penile deformation
History of NAION (use only if benefits outweigh risks) or 'crowded' optic disc
Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) - use not recommended
monitor: Blood pressure, especially with alpha-blockers or antihypertensives

preg: Tadalafil is not indicated for use in females. There are no human data to inform drug-associated risk in pregnancy. In animal reproduction studies, no teratogenicity, embryotoxicity, or fetotoxicity was observed in rats or mice during organogenesis at exposures up to 11 times the maximum recommended human dose (MRHD) of 20 mg/day. In rat prenatal/postnatal studies, decreased pup survival occurred at maternal exposures greater than ~10 times the MRHD; tadalafil and/or its metabolites cross the placenta in rats.
lact: Tadalafil is not indicated for use in females. There is no information on its presence in human milk, effects on the breastfed child, or effects on milk production. In lactating rats, tadalafil and/or its metabolites are present in milk at concentrations about 2.4-fold greater than in plasma.
renal: ED PRN, CrCl 30-50 mL/min: start at 5 mg not more than once daily, maximum 10 mg not more than once every 48 hours. ED PRN, CrCl <30 mL/min or on hemodialysis: maximum 5 mg not more than once every 72 hours. Once-daily ED: not recommended if CrCl <30 mL/min or on hemodialysis. BPH and ED/BPH, CrCl 30-50 mL/min: start at 2.5 mg, may increase to 5 mg based on response; if CrCl <30 mL/min or on hemodialysis, tadalafil is not recommended. Hemodialysis contributes negligibly to elimination.
hepatic: Mild or moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A or B): dosage adjustment may be needed and the dose should be used with caution. Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C): use of tadalafil is not recommended.

major: Organic nitrates in any form (nitroglycerin, isosorbide, amyl nitrite/'poppers') - CONTRAINDICATED; severe hypotension. If a nitrate is medically necessary, at least 48 hours should elapse after the last tadalafil dose, given only under close medical supervision with hemodynamic monitoring
Guanylate cyclase stimulators (riociguat) - CONTRAINDICATED; additive hypotension
Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, ritonavir, itraconazole) - increase tadalafil exposure; limit PRN dose to <=10 mg per 72 hours and once-daily dose to <=2.5 mg
moderate: Alpha-blockers (doxazosin, tamsulosin, alfuzosin) - additive blood-pressure lowering; not recommended with alpha-blockers for BPH; caution for ED
Antihypertensives (amlodipine, ARBs, bendrofluazide, enalapril, metoprolol) - small additive reductions in blood pressure
CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin) - decrease tadalafil exposure and may reduce efficacy
Other PDE5 inhibitors or PAH therapies - additive vasodilation; avoid concurrent use
minor: Antacids (magnesium/aluminum hydroxide) - reduce the rate of absorption without altering overall exposure (AUC)
H2 antagonists (e.g., nizatidine) - increased gastric pH; no clinically significant effect on exposure
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; the rate and extent of absorption of tadalafil are not influenced by food.
interactions.alcohol: Both tadalafil and alcohol are mild vasodilators. Substantial alcohol consumption (>=5 units) with tadalafil can increase orthostatic effects, including increased heart rate, decreased standing blood pressure, dizziness, and headache. Tadalafil and alcohol do not affect each other's plasma concentrations.
interactions.diagnostics: No routine laboratory monitoring required; assess cardiovascular status before prescribing. For BPH, evaluate for other urologic causes before starting.

common: Nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory tract infection (once-daily use)
serious: Symptomatic hypotension and syncope (especially with nitrates, alpha-blockers, antihypertensives, or alcohol)
Non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) - sudden vision loss in one or both eyes
Sudden decrease or loss of hearing, sometimes with tinnitus and dizziness
Serious cardiovascular events in patients with underlying cardiac risk
rare: Hypersensitivity reactions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome and exfoliative dermatitis
Diarrhea (more frequent in patients >=65 years on PRN dosing)
emergency: Erection lasting longer than 4 hours - seek immediate medical attention (priapism risk)
Sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes - stop drug and seek care (possible NAION)
Sudden decrease or loss of hearing - stop drug and seek prompt care
Anginal chest pain after dosing, or chest pain/severe dizziness/fainting during sexual activity - seek immediate care; do not take nitrates within 48 hours of tadalafil
Signs of severe skin reaction (blistering, peeling, mucosal involvement)

monitoring: Cardiovascular assessment before prescribing (rule out conditions where sexual activity is inadvisable)
Blood pressure, particularly when combined with alpha-blockers, antihypertensives, or alcohol
Vision changes (sudden loss may signal NAION)
Erection duration (>4 hours warrants emergency care)
For BPH: response and exclusion of other urologic conditions
counsel: For on-demand ED use, take before anticipated sexual activity; the effect can last up to 36 hours and requires sexual stimulation
For once-daily, BPH, ED/BPH, or PAH use, take at about the same time each day
Swallow the tablet whole - do not split it
NEVER use with nitrate medicines (e.g., nitroglycerin, isosorbide) or recreational nitrites ('poppers') - can cause dangerous drops in blood pressure
Do not use with riociguat (a guanylate cyclase stimulator)
Use no more than once per day for ED
Avoid large amounts of alcohol (5 or more units), which can cause dizziness, fainting, or a fast heartbeat
Seek emergency care for an erection lasting more than 4 hours
Stop the drug and seek care for sudden vision loss or sudden hearing loss
Tadalafil does not protect against sexually transmitted diseases including HIV
Tell your doctor about heart disease, recent heart attack/stroke, low or high blood pressure, liver or kidney problems, and all medicines including alpha-blockers
pk: Detectable effect from ~30 minutes (median Tmax 2 hours); requires sexual stimulation for ED
Plasma Cmax achieved 30 minutes to 6 hours after dosing (median 2 hours)
Mean terminal half-life ~17.5 hours in healthy subjects
Improves erectile function up to ~36 hours after an on-demand dose
Store at controlled room temperature 25 C (77 F); excursions permitted 15-30 C (59-86 F)
pearls: Absolutely contraindicated with nitrates in any form and with guanylate cyclase stimulators (riociguat) - life-threatening hypotension
Long ~17.5 h half-life gives effect up to 36 hours, distinguishing it from shorter-acting PDE5 inhibitors and enabling once-daily dosing
If a nitrate becomes medically necessary, wait at least 48 hours after the last tadalafil dose and give only under monitoring
Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, ritonavir, itraconazole): cap PRN at 10 mg/72 h and once-daily at 2.5 mg
Not recommended with alpha-blockers for BPH; use caution and lowest dose when treating ED in men on alpha-blockers
Renal limits: CrCl 30-50 reduce/space PRN dosing; CrCl <30 or dialysis cap PRN at 5 mg/72 h and avoid once-daily dosing
Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C): not recommended
Erection >4 hours is a urologic emergency (priapism); counsel on sudden vision/hearing loss
missed: For on-demand ED use, tadalafil is taken before sexual activity rather than on a schedule, so there is no missed-dose concern - simply take a dose when needed and never more than once daily. For once-daily ED, BPH, ED/BPH, or PAH use, take the missed dose when remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.
overdose: Single doses up to 500 mg in healthy subjects and repeated daily doses up to 100 mg in patients produced adverse events similar to those seen at lower doses. Management is standard supportive care. Hemodialysis contributes negligibly to tadalafil elimination, reflecting its high protein binding (94%) and predominantly fecal excretion.
